The provided text exhibits moderate cohesion, primarily relying on semantic relationships and logical progression rather than explicit transitional markers.

The first sentence, "State the name of the river that runs through London," is completely disconnected from the subsequent sentences. It lacks any lexical or thematic link to the topic of coral reefs and ocean acidification, creating a significant break in cohesion.

The remaining sentences, however, form a coherent paragraph. The transition from "Coral reefs are suffering due to ocean acidification" to "The increase in water temperature is also to blame" is effective. The use of the additive phrase "also to blame" clearly links the second cause (temperature) to the first (acidification), maintaining the focus on the factors damaging the reefs.

The shift to "Fish populations that depend on these reefs are declining" is logically sound. The phrase "these reefs" acts as a cohesive device, referring back to the coral reefs mentioned earlier, and establishes a cause-and-effect relationship between the environmental damage and the impact on marine life.

Finally, the sentence "This situation threatens not only marine life but also human communities that rely on fishing" serves as a strong concluding link. The demonstrative phrase "This situation" encapsulates the preceding points (acidification, temperature rise, and fish decline), while the structure "not only... but also" expands the scope of the impact from marine life to human communities, providing a logical and thematic closure to the paragraph.

In summary, while the first sentence is an outlier that disrupts the overall cohesion, the core paragraph demonstrates strong internal cohesion through clear logical progression, referential devices ("these reefs," "This situation"), and appropriate transitional phrases ("also to blame").
